Text only: the measure's stored vr_measures fields at audit time, no Congress.gov scrape. Filed rows are off-axis (the leaf's category is outside the act's dominant category before and after the row lands), is_primary false, weighted at the lowest weight the act's existing secondary rows already use. No issue key is created, no existing row is touched, no effect line is written.

H.R. 1968|119.title: Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
H.R. 1968|119.summary: Funded the federal government through the end of FY2025, trimming some domestic spending while boosting defense and immigration enforcement; averted a shutdown. Signed into law March 15, 2025.

H.R. 3746|118.title: Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023
H.R. 3746|118.summary: Division A sets discretionary spending caps for FY2024 and FY2025 enforced by sequestration. Division B rescinds unobligated balances including Internal Revenue Service funding and terminates the suspension of student loan payments and interest accrual. Division C modifies Temporary Assistance for Needy Families work requirements, raises the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program able-bodied-adults-without-dependents age limit to 54 while exempting homeless individuals, veterans and former foster youth, and enacts permitting reform limiting the scope of National Environmental Policy Act administrative review, with Sec. 324 ratifying all Mountain Valley Pipeline authorizations and exempting them from judicial review. Division D suspends the debt limit through January 1, 2025.

H.R. 1319|117.title: American Rescue Plan Act of 2021
H.R. 1319|117.summary: Provides additional relief to address the continued impact of COVID-19 on the economy, public health, state and local governments, individuals, and businesses. Includes direct payments, an expanded child tax credit, extended unemployment compensation, emergency rental and homeowner assistance, child care and Head Start funding, elementary and secondary school emergency relief, expanded Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, and the Restaurant Revitalization Fund.

H.R. 9770|119.title: Making continuing appropriations for fiscal year 2027, and for other purposes.
H.R. 9770|119.summary: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027. The bill provides continuing FY2027 appropriations to federal agencies through the earlier of December 4, 2026 or enactment of the applicable full-year appropriations act, preventing the shutdown that would otherwise begin when FY2027 starts on October 1, 2026. It funds most programs and activities at FY2026 levels, with anomalies providing funding flexibility or additional amounts for the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children, Small Business Administration loan programs, the Federal Emergency Management Agency's Disaster Relief Fund, the Indian Health Service and wildfire suppression. It extends expiring programs, authorities and restrictions, including the Department of Agriculture's livestock mandatory price reporting program, the National Flood Insurance Program, limits on pay increases for the Vice President and certain senior political appointees, the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program, authority to waive pay limitations for wildland firefighters and other wildland fire personnel, District of Columbia authority to spend local funds, and the freeze on cost-of-living adjustments for Members of Congress. It provides the customary payments to the beneficiaries of the late Representative David Scott and the late Senator Lindsey Graham. Passed the House 220-205 on July 22, 2026 (119/2 roll 272) and received in the Senate. Disambiguation: the corpus previously held only this measure's official title, "Making continuing appropriations for fiscal year 2027, and for other purposes" — the short title as passed is "Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027". It is a continuing resolution and not a full-year appropriations act; H.R. 8595 in the same Congress is the FY2027 national security and State Department appropriations bill and a separate vehicle.

S. 2296|119.title: S. 2296 — National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026
S. 2296|119.summary: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 as reported by the Senate Armed Services Committee and passed by the Senate on October 10, 2025 (119/1 roll 570). It sets FY2026 policies and authorities for Department of Defense programs and activities, military construction and the national security programs of the Department of Energy, and authorizes the Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board for FY2026; it authorizes appropriations but does not provide budget authority. Among other elements it authorizes procurement of aircraft, ships and missiles, authorizes active-duty and reserve personnel strength levels, authorizes military construction projects, requires a strategy on the national security implications of emerging biotechnologies, requires the Navy to improve the material condition and combat readiness of surface ships maintained at private shipyards, extends the Pacific Deterrence Initiative through FY2026, and repeals statutory provisions on diversity, equity and inclusion within the Department including the position of Chief Diversity Officer. Disambiguation: S. 2296 and S. 1071 carry the same title. S. 1071 is the vehicle that became Public Law 119-60; S. 2296 was held at the desk on November 12, 2025 and was never enacted, and it carries roughly thirty short titles for portions of the bill.

S.Amdt. 1354|118.title: Kennedy amendment prohibiting VA reporting of fiduciary determinations to NICS
S.Amdt. 1354|118.summary: Second-degree amendment to the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies appropriations division of H.R. 4366, offered by Senator John Kennedy: "To prohibit the availability of funds for the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to report certain information to the Department of Justice for use by the National Instant Criminal Background Check System." Agreed to 53-45 on 2023-10-25 with eleven Democrats voting yea. Enacted as Section 413 of Division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2024 (P.L. 118-42, 138 Stat. 65), which bars the use of Division A funds to report to the Attorney General, for NICS purposes, that a person deemed mentally incapacitated, mentally incompetent or experiencing an extended loss of consciousness has been adjudicated a mental defective under 18 U.S.C. 922(d)(4) and (g)(4), unless a judicial authority has found that the person is a danger to themselves or others.
